title: Psalm 62: My Soul Finds Rest in God Alone
summary: David declares that his soul waits quietly for God alone, his rock, salvation, and fortress, while enemies try to topple him with lies. He calls the people to trust God and pour out their hearts to him, warns that human status and wealth are only a breath, and closes with a twofold word he has heard: power belongs to God, and so does loving devotion.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 64
from.text: Psalm 64 closes the small group of Davidic trust psalms in 61 to 64 and is the last lament before the three great songs of praise in Psalms 65 to 67.

line: David waits quietly for God alone, his rock and fortress, while enemies try to topple him with lies, and calls the people to pour out their hearts to God.
guide: Rest here means stopping the inner struggle and trusting God with it, and the psalmist has to tell his own soul to do it. Take the invitation of verse 8 and pour out everything, not tidy prayers. Then ask what you lean your heart on that weighs less than a breath.

stanzas.title: My soul rests in God alone
Enemies who push, lie, and curse in secret
The soul told again to rest in God
An invitation to the people: pour out your hearts
People are a breath, riches are no refuge
Power and loving devotion belong to God

verses.t: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. In God alone my soul finds rest; my salvation comes from Him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation. He is my fortress; I will never be shaken.
How long will you threaten a man? Will all of you throw him down like a leaning wall or a tottering fence?
They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch; they delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah
Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be shaken.
My salvation and my honor rest on God, my strong rock; my refuge is in God.
Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah
Lowborn men are but a vapor, the exalted but a lie. Weighed on the scale, they go up; together they are but a vapor.
Place no trust in extortion, or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.
God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God,
and loving devotion to You, O Lord. For You will repay each man according to his deeds.
